author: nyc gazette
title: St. John's extends winning streak to seven after victory over Butler - NYC Gazette
text:
The St. John’s Red Storm men’s basketball team secured a 92-70 win over Butler at Madison Square Garden on Wednesday, extending their winning streak to seven games. With this victory, the team improved its record to 16-5 overall and 9-1 in the Big East Conference for the second consecutive year.
St. John’s, based in Queens, New York, is part of the Big East Conference and has a history that includes six Big East Tournament titles and two NIT championships according to their official website . The Red Storm have now won 25 of their last 27 regular season conference games, joining Akron and Duke as the only NCAA Division I programs with at least 25 league wins in that span.
During Wednesday’s game, St. John’s overcame an early struggle from three-point range but finished by making nine of their last thirteen attempts from beyond the arc. The team shot 56.3 percent from the field in front of more than 14,000 fans.
Senior forward Dillon Mitchell recorded his third double-double in four games with 14 points and a season-high 13 rebounds. He also contributed four assists and matched his season high with three blocks. Over his last four appearances, Mitchell has averaged 14.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game.
Sophomore guard Ian Jackson led St. John’s with 18 points and was perfect from the free throw line on five attempts. Zuby Ejiofor added 15 points on efficient shooting along with six rebounds, five assists, and three blocks. Joson Sanon scored 13 points for St. John’s while hitting all three of his shots from long distance.
For Butler, Michael Ajayi posted a game-high of 19 points and collected eleven rebounds.
The Red Storm opened the contest with a strong start that included a highlight alley-oop play between Bryce Hopkins and Dillon Mitchell during a decisive early run that put them ahead by fourteen points midway through the first half.
Butler narrowed the gap late in the first half before St. John’s responded by hitting five consecutive three-pointers to take a fourteen-point lead into halftime.
In the second half, St. John’s maintained control and built its advantage to as much as twenty-nine points before closing out its second conference win by more than twenty points this season.
St. John’s will not play again until Tuesday when they face DePaul at Wintrust Arena in Chicago for an evening matchup.
More information about St. John’s Red Storm Men’s Basketball—including its participation in college basketball competition within the Big East Conference—can be found on their official website .
